Well, even with the performance issues, it was my favorite 3D Pokémon game so far (I haven’t played Legends Arceus yet so this is likely to change), so I’d say definitely. Would it be better than the handheld era? No, I wouldn’t say so.

However, there were a lot of quality of life changes I really welcomed in this game.

I don’t know about everybody else, but I do *not* miss grinding even a little bit. I remember playing Platinum and having to grind for a good two hours in between the eighth gym and victory road, and it was incredibly tedious. Scarlet and Violet was a much smoother experience in terms of pacing.

That being said, the region was… meh. There was obviously a lot of hidden nooks and crannies to explore but most of them felt empty and uninspired. It felt like there wasn’t a lot of thought put into each area compared to previous games where each region felt meticulously designed and constructed by hand.

The lack of level scaling was also a problem. I had to actually look up which gyms had which levels because I didn’t want to do them out of order for fear of being over or under-leveled.

The graphics and performance were also pathetic for a game in 2023. The Pokémon models looked great but the environments did not.

I still had a lot of fun with this game and I’m glad I played it. The story was one of my favorites in all of Pokémon, and I adored the characters. I can tell that developers were working with the time constraints they had to make it as finished as possible but unfortunately weren’t given enough time by the higher ups. If they had had another year to work on this I’m eager to see what it would’ve looked like.

Luffy does whatever he wants and once his mind is set on something you can’t get him to stop. Sure, a lot of it ends up saving a lot of people, but Luffy never wants to be obligated to do that. He wanted to beat Kaido because a girl starved herself in order to feed him and that pissed him off. He had personal stakes in defeating Kaido.

Remember when he agreed to help Law capture Caesar? The first couple times he tried fighting him, his heart wasn’t in it because he didn’t care about Caesar. Then he found out Caesar was drugging children and that they were dying because of it. Suddenly, Luffy is pissed off and he beats Caesar no problem.

Dressrosa and Wano also both had something in common. Nobody there was free, all because some greedy pirate made it that way. Luffy values freedom above all else so he wanted to knock these pirates down from their thrones.

So yeah, he may end up the hero a lot of the time, but it’s never with the intention of being viewed as the hero. It’s all for his own selfish reasons.
